```{r setup}
.libPaths(path.expand("~/MMM/renv/library/linux-ubuntu-noble/R-4.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"))
REG <- read.csv(path.expand("~/MMM/tables/V4_S7_numbers.csv"), colClasses = "character", na.strings = NULL)
TRACE <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("MMM_S7_TRACE"))
n <- function(id) {
  i <- which(REG$id == id)
  if (length(i) != 1) stop("registry id not found once: ", id)
  if (TRACE) "\u00a7" else REG$text[i]
}
```

This supplement accompanies the manuscript. Every number is read from the same registry of values as the main text. GB = GenBinaryY, NAT = GLMM-native, AR1 = GLMM-AR1; MMM = marginalized multilevel model.

## S1. Parameters of the data-generating mechanisms

**Table S1.** Parameters under the alternative, read from the table extracted from the executed code. Under the null only the interaction coefficient is set to zero. Coefficients are in the order (Intercept), time, trt, covariate if any, time:trt; they are marginal for GenBinaryY, conditional for GLMM-native and the marginal target for GLMM-AR1, whose conditional coefficients are calibrated on each replicate.

## S4. Numerical behaviour of the small-sample corrections

The corrections of Mancl and DeRouen, Kauermann and Carroll and Fay and Graubard were computed with `geesmv`. On sparse binary data with few clusters the three functions can loop indefinitely in compiled code, so each call ran in a separate process killed after `r n("x:geesmv_timeout")` seconds; the largest share of time-outs in a cell was `r n("x:to_max")`%. In the earlier version of this work the Kauermann-Carroll correction appeared to shrink rather than inflate the variance; recomputing the three corrections from the estimating-equation building blocks showed that this was a property of the implementation, which refits the model internally and applies a symmetric matrix square root to a non-symmetric matrix, and not of the estimator. The hand computation of Fay-Graubard agreed with the package at every grid point checked. These checks are documented with the code.
